subject: check DSCR assumptions early
preheader: modeled financing and lender terms are not the same thing.
headline: A DSCR screen is a prompt to verify lender-specific terms.
body: Consider a hypothetical duplex listed at $325,000 with $1,650 monthly rent per unit. A preliminary screen can calculate cap rate, cash flow, and DSCR from the rent, expense, price, and financing assumptions entered.

Now suppose the screen uses 75% loan-to-value while a prospective lender requires more cash down or applies a different qualifying rate and expense method. Those changes can materially alter modeled debt service, DSCR, and cash-on-cash return.

An illustrative 1.09 DSCR would miss a hypothetical 1.25 threshold, but neither number predicts a real lender's terms or approval. Each lender defines qualifying income, expenses, reserves, and minimum coverage for the specific borrower and property.
The lesson is to validate financing assumptions before relying on the screen, not to treat a consumer calculation as the lender's analysis or an investment verdict.
TrueCap makes the financing and operating assumptions editable so you can identify what to confirm with the lender and other qualified professionals.
